standard_applied.exit_gate: nothing intersects the subsystem WITHOUT BEING EXPLICITLY BOUNDED -- bounded, not absent
standard_applied.linter: phase4_promotion_preflight.py reads a hand-declared `bounded_residuals` list; each entry needs boundary + evidence + next_experiment and intersects_dimension: false

method.two_discharge_bases_are_NOT_equivalent: BOUNDED_DOCUMENTED_EXTENT rests on a cited element count. BOUNDED_NEGATIVE_INDEX rests on the convention that array indices are non-negative -- the same assumption region_provenance.c's TIER 2 discloses. They are counted separately because merging them would inflate the stronger basis with the weaker one.
method.index_magnitude: The quantity that decides intersection is not whether an index is bounded in the abstract, but how large it would have to be to land in the target window.
method.extent_bound: From a documented extent where Canon has one, else from the nearest distinct base observed above the object.
method.RETRACTED_adjacency_argument: An earlier version bounded objects by the distance to the nearest distinct base above them. That is NOT a bounding argument: the median such distance is 4 bytes, because consecutive bases are usually sibling FIELDS of one array element, not the start of a different object. It discharged 4,730 of 4,911 sites for the wrong reason and was removed before it was banked.
method.runtime_cross_check: A readwrite watch over boot -> frontend -> Clover Forest observed exactly 7 PCs touching these tables (analysis/phase4_e16_table_read_watch.json), none of them from any residual cluster.

extent_claims_refuted_by_proven_index._why: Every claimed extent is checked against the largest index the analyser can PROVE at that same base. A claim smaller than the demonstrated reach is refuted and discharges nothing.

extent_evidence_audit._why: An extent is only as good as where it came from. Two of fourteen claims are independently corroborated by a proven (non-width-cast) index at the same base; the rest are unverified in BOTH directions -- the analyser has no independent index there at all.

extent_evidence_audit.one_claim_was_imported_from_outside_the_: 0x8009FBE8 was first claimed as 24*16 = 384 B because 'the SPU has 24 voices'. The codebase says 32: _SsVmInit 0x800699F8 zero-fills 32 entries of 2 bytes. General knowledge about the hardware is not evidence about THIS program.

the_next_object_bound_as_ONE_named_resid._why: This basis discharges 161 clusters. Declaring it as 161 evidenced boundaries would be the same inflation the non-negative-index convention was pulled out of: it is ONE systematic argument.
the_next_object_bound_as_ONE_named_resid.boundary: Accesses whose object has a distinct neighbouring object starting within 1 KB above it, where reaching an E16 window would need at least 10x that distance.
the_next_object_bound_as_ONE_named_resid.evidence: Bases are first clustered into OBJECTS (gap < 0x100), because the naive `nearest distinct base` version was retracted -- its median gap is 4 bytes, since adjacent bases are usually sibling FIELDS. Unconstrained the clustered version discharges 100% of the residual, which is the tautology signature; its tight-margin cases (ratio 1.0x) are exactly those where NO neighbour was observed for 12-18 KB, so the `extent` is a GAP, not a bound. Constraining it to a real neighbour within 1 KB AND a 10x margin keeps only the cases where the argument means something.
the_next_object_bound_as_ONE_named_resid.next_experiment: Watch the E16 windows across the per-level campaign; a write from a base whose object has a close neighbour would falsify the no-overlap assumption this rests on.

the_non_negative_index_convention_as_ONE._why: 722 of 851 priority discharges rest on this single convention. Spread across 722 line items it reads like 722 independent findings; it is one assumption, and it belongs in the packet as one residual.
the_non_negative_index_convention_as_ONE.boundary: Accesses whose region base lies ABOVE the target window. Reaching the window from them requires a NEGATIVE index.
the_non_negative_index_convention_as_ONE.evidence: MAGNITUDE is what makes this sound, and it was measured rather than assumed (analysis/phase4_e16_signed_index_audit.json). Of the 2,922 accesses discharged this way, ZERO need a small (<64) negative index; 47 need 64-1k and 2,875 need >= 1k. The convention is not being asked to rule out an off-by-one -- it is ruling out an array running hundreds to thousands of elements BACKWARDS past its own base. 27.5% of the indices are signed-CAPABLE (lh, sra, subu, the sll16/sra16 short cast), but not one of them is asked to be even slightly negative. Same disclosed convention as region_provenance.c TIER 2.
the_non_negative_index_convention_as_ONE.known_exception_class_RESOLVED: 0x8005D69C computes 0x800A6300 + (short)a3*4, a SIGNED short index -- the site that made this residual un-assertable. It is based BELOW its target, so it is not among the sites this convention discharges at all, and the measured risk set (small negative index AND not provably non-negative) is EMPTY.
the_non_negative_index_convention_as_ONE.next_experiment: Watch all three table windows with a readwrite accessLog across a campaign of per-level replays. Any write arriving from a base above a window falsifies this. One run (boot -> frontend -> Clover Forest) already passed: 7 PCs observed, none from a base above the window.

HOW_MUCH_WEIGHT_EACH_BASIS_CARRIES._why: A headline count of discharged sites hides which basis did the work. Here the weakest one does almost all of it, and that must be visible in the packet rather than discoverable only by re-deriving it.
HOW_MUCH_WEIGHT_EACH_BASIS_CARRIES.comparison: B06's committed frontier used the same convention for 6 of its 165 exclusions. Here it carries 722 of 807 discharges (89%). Same disclosed basis, completely different load-bearing weight.
